speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me how long the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction has been continuing, and does it happen with just light pressure? Also, can you describe the size and frequency of the bruises you've been getting lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your uncle's history of joint swelling and bleeding, do you or your family members have a diagnosis of hemophilia or another bleeding disorder? Have you noticed any bleeding into your joints or prolonged bleeding after other minor injuries or surgeries in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall if any other male relatives in your family have experienced similar bleeding or joint issues, and have you ever had bleeding into your joints after minor trauma? Given this strong family history, I would like to order some specific blood work to check your clotting factors. REQUEST TEST: aPTT, PT, Fibrinogen, Factor VIII, Factor IX.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hematologic Panel - Hematocrit: 35%, Leukocyte Count: 8,500/mm3, Platelet Count: 160,000/mm3, Prothrombin Time (PT): 15 sec, Partial Thromboplastin Time (aPTT): 60 sec, Bleeding Time: 6 min, Fibrin Split Products: Negative, Peripheral Blood Smear: Normal-sized platelets. Serum Chemistries - Urea Nitrogen: 20 mg/dL, Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL, Total Bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.5 mg/dL, Lactate Dehydrogenase: 90 U/L. Note: Specific Factor VIII, Factor IX, and Fibrinogen levels were not included in the provided data; however, the aPTT is prolonged

speaker: Doctor
text: Your lab results show a prolonged aPTT with normal platelets and PT, which strongly suggests an intrinsic pathway defect like Hemophilia A or B. To confirm the specific deficiency, I need to see your Factor VIII and Factor IX levels, so I will order those tests now. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Assay, Factor IX Assay.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your Factor VIII and IX levels are normal despite the prolonged aPTT, could you tell me if you have ever experienced severe bleeding after minor surgeries or if you have noticed any symptoms suggesting von Willebrand disease, such as frequent nosebleeds? I will now request a specific test for von Willebrand factor to investigate further. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity, Factor VIII Activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged aPTT with normal Factor VIII, IX, and von Willebrand factor levels, I suspect a rare factor deficiency like Factor XI or XII. Do you recall any history of bleeding after dental work or minor cuts, and has anyone in your family been diagnosed with a rare bleeding disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your Factor VIII, IX, and von Willebrand factor levels are normal, could you confirm if you or your uncle have ever been diagnosed with Factor XI deficiency (Hemophilia C), which is common in certain populations? I will now request a specific test to check your Factor XI levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Assay.

speaker: Doctor
text: With Factor XI also normal, I suspect an inhibitor or Factor XII deficiency; do you have any history of recurrent miscarriages in female relatives or unexplained thrombosis? REQUEST TEST: Factor XII Assay, Lupus Anticoagulant, Factor VIII Inhibitor Titer.

speaker: Doctor
text: With the aPTT prolonged but all specific factor levels and inhibitor tests normal, I suspect a rare deficiency like Factor XI or an artifact; however, given your uncle's history of joint swelling, could you confirm if you have ever had hemarthrosis (bleeding into joints)? I will request a mixing study to see if the prolonged aPTT corrects with normal plasma. REQUEST TEST: aPTT Mixing Study.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Factor XII Deficiency (Hageman Factor Deficiency)
